Cyber Attack Disrupts Brazilian Metals & Mining Firms, Operations Halted

A major cyber attack targeting Brazil's metals and mining sector has forced several leading companies to suspend operations, industry officials confirmed Wednesday. The incident, believed to be a sophisticated ransomware assault, has disrupted critical IT systems and halted production at key sites in Minas Gerais and Pará states.

The attack began late Tuesday, encrypting company data and demanding payment in cryptocurrency to restore access, according to a spokesperson for Grupo FerroSul, one of the affected firms. "Our teams are working around the clock to restore systems and assess the extent of the breach," said Chief Information Officer Renata Vieira. "Production at our Itabira and Carajás facilities is currently paused as a precaution."

The Brazilian Mining Association estimates that at least four mid-to-large mining companies have been impacted so far, with combined daily output losses reaching up to 60,000 tonnes of iron ore and 4,000 tonnes of copper. "This is a significant disruption to Brazil's metals supply chain," said Ricardo Farias, an analyst at Instituto Minerar. "If downtime extends beyond 48 hours, we could see notable effects on both domestic supply and export schedules."

The National Union of Mining Workers has expressed concern for employee safety and job security as plants remain offline. "We urge companies to communicate transparently and prioritize worker protection," union president Elisa Campos said.

The attack underscores growing cyber risks in the resource sector, where digital infrastructure is increasingly critical to operations. As of Wednesday afternoon, companies and government agencies continue to investigate the source and scope of the breach, with no timeline yet for full restoration of services.
